VERDICT: LGTM

The new `formatCheckDigit(Owner)` method slots cleanly into the existing family of `format*(Owner)` default methods on `OwnerMapper` and follows every established convention in the file:

- It mirrors the sibling `formatMembershipNumber`, which also derives its value from `customerCode`, so deriving the check digit from the same source in the same unit is the natural home — a maintainer would expect to find it here.
- The `@Mapping(target = "checkDigit", ...)` entry is placed in the same expression-based block as the other derived fields, consistent with the rest of the mapping.
- Null-handling (`owner == null || owner.getCustomerCode() == null → null`) matches the guard style and the documented rationale pattern used by `formatMembershipNumber` and the others.
- Javadoc density/tone matches the surrounding methods, and the self-contained Luhn loop introduces no duplication (no existing check-digit logic to reuse).
- The OpenAPI schema addition is additive and placed adjacently to the related `customerCode`/`membershipNumber` properties with the same style (`readOnly`, title/description/example).

No class or method is becoming a catch-all here — the mapper already owns this family of DTO-derivation helpers, and this is one more of the same kind.
